## Project timeline

Delivered scope spans inception to the 2026.01-rc3 release. Each step carries its tracking issue. Every item below closed as a tested pull request and verified by execution; the dates are the issue-close dates.

**3 October — baseline**

- The product specification was written and reviewed before implementation. The repository, CI, governance documents and website followed ([#1](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/1), [#37](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/37)-[#56](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/56)).

**8 October — first capabilities**

- The rule engine runs a security rule against a test request and returns a verdict — the core decision loop, verified by fixtures ([#2](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/2), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/59)).
- The kernel packet filter compiles, loads under the verifier and detaches cleanly — the eBPF environment is proven ([#3](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/3), gate output in [lab](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/lab/README.md)).

**9 October — packet path verified end to end**

- The kernel-to-engine event channel passes its end-to-end test in the lab: packets become structured events with the correct field layout ([#4](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/4), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/81)).
- Requests score stage-by-stage (the inspection ladder), with verdicts recorded at each stage ([#5](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/5)).
- HTTP request bodies parse into the structured view the rules operate on ([#5](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/5), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/88)).

**10 October — v0.1**

(Renamed to 2026.01-rc1 at the same commit.)

- The deployment lab reproduces on demand: cluster, gateway, firewall and a demo application. Each network hop verifies by response headers ([#6](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/6), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/96)).
- The firewall's verdicts match the vendor-neutral reference rule set (OWASP CRS) on every corpus case — 19/19, with one documented gap. The CI enforces the comparison on all future changes ([#7](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/7), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/103)).
- A security policy written as a Kubernetes resource is compiled and loaded by the platform. Matching traffic is blocked. The apply-to-effect round trip measures 1.5–2.6 s within the 5 s budget ([#8](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/8), PRs [#98](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/98)/[#104](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/104)).
- Repeat offenders are dropped in the kernel, bans expire automatically, and every ban produces an evidence record ([#10](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/10), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/105)).
- Every verdict emits three correlated records — trace, metric, log — tied by request id ([#11](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/11), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/101)).
- Automated clients are distinguishable from browsers by traffic fingerprints, validated against published test vectors ([#12](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/12), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/99)).
- A route's published API schema acts as an allow-list: non-conforming requests are rejected with a diagnostic naming the violated field ([#13](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/13), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/102)).
- The platform's limits are stated, not implied: the README exit checklist marks each acceptance criterion pass or pending with evidence links ([#14](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/14), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/108)). The release is signed and published ([2026.01-rc1](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/releases/tag/2026.01-rc1)).

**23 October — 2026.01-rc2**

- Requests parse across HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and gRPC into one structured view ([#15](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/15), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/138)).
- The CEL graph reloads rules on apply and holds each rule under its cost budget ([#17](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/17), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/134)).
- Automated-client detection grows behavioural windows over the JA4 fingerprints ([#19](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/19)).
- Rate limiting runs token-bucket, sliding-window and EWMA algorithms per route ([#20](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/20), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/141)).
- The bench gate reads per-row budget verdicts in the serialized CI fleet ([#24](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/24), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/144), [#150](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/150)).
- Release artefacts carry build-provenance attestations and an SBOM ([#81](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/81), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/139)). The release is signed and published ([2026.01-rc2](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/releases/tag/2026.01-rc2)).

**24 October — 2026.01-rc3**

- Behavioural DoS detectors land as shadowed shapes: the kernel counts per-flow window features, the engine classifies slowloris and rapid-reset ([#31](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/31), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/225)).
- The engine gains its TLS-termination secondary mode, fail-closed on a split pair ([#34](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/34), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/218)).
- The build ships multi-arch with OpenShift compatibility notes ([#33](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/33), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/215)).
- The uninstall residue gate asserts zero kernel leftovers after live teardown in CI ([#35](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/35), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/186)).
- The socket-plane compiler lands its first class: route marking compiles end to end, the verifier gate runs in CI, the shadow differential pins the mismatch budget ([#52](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/52), PRs [#200](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/200), [#207](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/207), [#212](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/212)).
- The declarative layer moves to CUE with a golden-diff gate against hand edits ([#46](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/192), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/222)).
- The Academy ships modules 1, 3, 4 and 2, 5 ([#27](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/27), [#28](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/28), PRs [#178](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/178), [#210](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/210)).
- The tracked evaluations publish: HTTP/3 ingress posture, the DPU port, the composition watch ([#29](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/29), [#32](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/32), [#36](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/36)).
- The release is signed and published ([2026.01-rc3](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/releases/tag/2026.01-rc3)).

## What is left

The releases carry honest caps. The remaining gaps, stated:

- The route-class fast path reads as a tracked evaluation; more policy classes ride later slices ([#52](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/52)).
- Verdicts export OTLP over the wire later; the triad verifies in-memory today ([#11](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/11)).
- Engine-only cells measure in CI today; inline walls under 10 ms ride the 2026.01 GA bucket ([#24](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/24)).
- The next release is the GA cut: the bare `2026.01` name, per [ADR-0003](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-release-naming.md).

## Sprint sequencing

The 2026.01-rc1 sprint sequence: shield PoC → ingest → ladder slice → NGF steering lab → CRS differential → operator/CRD round-trip → ScoredWindowBan → OTel pipeline → bot v0 → positive security v0 → honest exit ([TR-14](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/14)).

## Contributing

Contributions follow the [contributing guide](contributing.html). Pick an issue labelled `complexity:starter`, or any `area:*` that fits. The issue body carries the design source. Branch + PR against `trishula-dev/trishula` (MIT).
